Raghaṭ occurs once in the plural in the Atharvaveda, where the Paippalāda recension reads vaghaṭah. Roth once con jectured raghavaḥ, ‘swift,’ as the correct reading. Bloomfield, who in his translation explains the word as ‘falcons,’ in his notes inclines to think Roth's conjecture likely. Ludwig suggests ‘bees’ as the meaning. Possibly some kind of bird may be intended.
Foot notes viii. 7, 24.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v., 1a.
